newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka in $3.5 billion plan to develop south.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka in $3.5 billion plan to develop south.

text.p: Sri Lanka is to launch an ambitious $3.5 billion development plan with private sector participation to tame its volatile south, a senior government official said on Thursday.

"The first phase of the plan involves mega-infrastructure projects which will require an investment of $3.5 billion within three to five years," said Navin Gooneratne, chairman and director general of the Southern Development Authority (SDA).
The SDA is putting the finishing touches on the plan, which will be presented to the cabinet next week.
The SDA was set up to develop the southern Ruhunu region, which has been a breeding ground for two revolts in the past 25 years due to high unemployment.
"The south has a wealth of highly literate youth between the ages of 18 to 27 years who do not have jobs," Gooneratne said.
He said unemployment in the region averaged 20 percent compared to a national average of around 13.
The SDA plan revolves round the creation of a city called Ruhunupura spread over 68,000 hectares (168,025 acres), said Gooneratne, one of Sri Lanka's leading architects.

Ruhunupura in the sourthern Hambantota district 238 km (150 miles) from Colombo, will have a modern port and airport and be connected to the capital by an express road and rail link, which form the bulk of development under phase one.
"We have already signed a joint venture agreement with a U.S./Canadian consortium to invest up to $1 billion in phase one," he said.
Gooneratne declined to identify the participants in the consortium, saying it was premature to do so as final details of the agreement were being worked out.
Phase two, which involves attracting investment to create jobs, has already seen German firms Krupp Udhe GMbh and MPC Munchmeyer GMbh committing $25 million dollars to build a caustic soda factory.
"We have also signed 40 joint venture agreements with local entrepreneurs who will slot into phase two," he said.
SDA will hold a minority interest in all joint ventures and its contribution will be real estate, Gooneratne said.
The SDA expects to fully implement its plan by 2001.
